account:
Today I have been following my appointments: morning office business, the ten o'clock mill inspection, and now lunch at home before council letters at thirteen hundred. The mill had 76 hay bales in its stock chest, so I saw no obvious shortage there. Freight suggested better lighting at both ferry landings and marked waiting areas away from the water; I asked the secretary to record those practical improvements.

There seems to be some quiet coordination among the local tradespeople. Yesterday I saw the builder give planks and a lantern to the baker. Today several townsfolk repeated talk of a 'bridge or port change' at the bakery, naming the baker, builder, innkeeper, freight, and neighbour in various combinations. These reports were vague, not a definite proposal. When I visited, I found the neighbour and innkeeper. The innkeeper said he knew of no proposal and was only following up an inn bread order; he asked me to tell the baker or freight he was looking for them. The neighbour said the baker and freight had recently been there and the baker had fresh bread to deliver, but could not give a reliable direction.

The clearest unusual business is this evening's civic presentation. My signed appointment supplement describes an appreciation of municipal public service organised by the inn and local tradespeople, from eighteen hundred to eighteen thirty in the great hall. It says I approved it yesterday, supersedes an earlier pending request, and specifically asks me not to arrive before eighteen hundred because the organisers need time to finish arrangements around their work. I also heard the secretary say she would keep its contents private. That makes me suspect the quiet gatherings, bread orders, and perhaps the supplies are preparations for a surprise appreciation event, rather than evidence of an actual bridge or port scheme. I cannot yet establish that connection, and I should not treat the rumours as facts. I intend to keep my remaining appointments, including tea with the neighbour at fifteen hundred and arriving at the presentation precisely at eighteen hundred.
